SL.GDP.PCAP.EM.KD.label: GDP per person employed
SL.GDP.PCAP.EM.KD.unit: constant PPP $ (base year in API name)

wdi.source: World Bank WDI API v2 (ILO modelled estimates for employment)

findings: In 2025, agriculture employed 41.6% of workers in India but produced 16.2% of GDP as value added — a gap of -25.4 percentage points.
In 2025, value added per worker in services was 3.9× that in agriculture, and in industry 2.5× (ratios of relative labour productivity: services 1.52, industry 0.98, agriculture 0.39).
In 2025, the three sector value-added shares sum to 90.8% of GDP; the remaining 9.2% is net taxes on products and other adjustments, not a sector.
Agriculture's share of employment went from 63.1% in 1991 to 41.6% in 2025 (-21.5 pp), while its value-added share went from 27.7% to 16.2% (-11.4 pp).
Manufacturing value added was 13.5% of GDP in 2025, -4.4 pp from its highest level in the selected years (17.9% in 1995).
In 2025, 32.4% of women aged 15+ in India were in the labour force against 77.6% of men — a gap of 45.2 pp (ILO modelled estimates).
In 2025, 71.6% of India's workers were in vulnerable employment (own-account or contributing family work; ILO modelled estimate).
